The director gave everyone a copy of the script.

easy.def: The holy writings of a religion.
examples: We read scripture at church.
The scripture is old.
A line of scripture.

more.def: The holy writings of a religion, such as the Bible.
examples: We read a line of scripture at the start of the service.
Each religion has its own scripture, written long ago.
The priest read from the scripture.

easy.def: A long paper rolled up.
examples: The scroll was very old.
He unrolled the scroll.
A scroll hung on the wall.

more.def: A long roll of paper or parchment with writing on it.
examples: The museum had an ancient scroll in a glass case.
He unrolled the scroll and read the message aloud.
People once wrote books on long scrolls instead of pages.

easy.def: To move text on a screen up or down.
examples: I scroll down the page.
Scroll to the top.
She scrolled through the pictures.

more.def: To move what is on a computer or phone screen up or down to see more.
examples: I scrolled down the page to find the answer.
He scrolled through the photos on the tablet.
Scroll to the top of the page to start again.

easy.def: To search and gather things that people do not want.
examples: We scrounged for snacks.
He scrounged for wood.
She scrounged in the closet.

more.def: To search around and gather things that other people have thrown away or do not need.
examples: We scrounged for old boards to build a fort.
He scrounged in the closet for a flashlight.
The raccoons scrounged for food in the trash.

easy.def: To rub hard to clean.
examples: I scrub the pot.
She scrubbed the floor.
Scrub your hands.

more.def: To rub something hard with a brush to get it clean.
examples: I scrubbed the muddy boots.
She scrubbed the pot until it shone.
Scrub your hands with soap before dinner.

related.def: A brush or pad for scrubbing.

easy.def: To crush or squeeze up.
examples: I scrunch my nose.
She scrunched the paper.
He scrunched up his face.

more.def: To squeeze or crumple something into a tight shape.
examples: I scrunched my nose at the smell.
She scrunched the paper into a ball.
He scrunched up his face at the sour taste.

easy.def: Gear with a tank of air for swimming deep underwater.
examples: We went scuba diving.
A scuba tank holds air.
He learned scuba.

more.def: Equipment with a tank of air that lets a person breathe while swimming deep under the water.
examples: She learned to scuba dive so she could see the coral reef.
The scuba tank on his back held air for an hour.
A scuba diver explored the sunken ship.

easy.def: To make a statue by shaping clay, stone or wood.
examples: I sculpt with clay.
She sculpted a bird.
He sculpted a horse.

more.def: To shape a figure from clay, stone, wood or another material.
examples: She sculpted a bird out of clay.
The artist sculpted a horse from stone.
We sculpted animals from soft clay in art class.

easy.def: An artist who makes statues.
examples: The sculptor made a statue.
A sculptor uses clay.
She is a sculptor.

more.def: An artist who makes figures from clay, stone, wood or metal.
examples: The sculptor carved a bear from a block of wood.
A sculptor shaped the statue from clay.
The sculptor worked on the marble for months.

easy.def: A piece of art that is carved or made into a shape.
examples: The sculpture was made of clay.
We saw a sculpture.
The sculpture is tall.

more.def: A piece of art made by carving, shaping or joining things such as stone, clay or metal.
examples: The sculpture was carved from a block of stone.
We saw a giant metal sculpture in the park.
She made a clay sculpture of her cat.

easy.def: To run fast with small steps.
examples: Mice scurry away.
The squirrel scurried up the tree.
The ants scurried.

more.def: To run quickly with short, quick steps.
examples: The mouse scurried across the kitchen floor.
Children scurried to their seats when the bell rang.
Little crabs scurried across the sand.

easy.def: To run fast with small steps.
examples: The crab will scuttle away.
Mice scuttled across the floor.
A bug scuttled under the rug.

more.def: To run quickly with short steps, the way a crab or a mouse does.
examples: The little crab scuttled sideways across the sand.
A beetle scuttled under a leaf when the light came on.
The mice scuttled back into their hole.
